newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity seen flat, Intertie hike delayed.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity seen flat, Intertie hike delayed.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were expected to open flat to lower Monday amid news that a 1,050 megawatt (MW) capacity increase on a key transmission line to move cheap hydropower to the Southwest was postponed.
Last Friday, the Western Systems Coordinating Council approved to boost the capacity of Pacific Intertie by about 25 percent to 6,250 MW from 5,200 MW.

Bonneville Power Adminstration (BPA), which operates the line with Pacific Gas and Electric Co, said it will not be able to immediately raise the capacity of the intertie because of a problem on a 500 kilovolt segment of the line. The North-South power flow on the transmission line would have ramped up this weekend.
No estimate was available for when the 500 KV line would be back in service.
"I think if it's back before April 1, it'll be okay," said an East Coast electricity broker, noting the postponement, if brief, would have little effect on the market.
"I think it would make the market go higher, but over-the-counter (prices) is unchanged to a little lower," said one New York futures broker, referring to the delay.

In over-the-counter business, April California-Oregon Border (COB) futures were quoted at $10.20-10.40 a megawatt hour (MWh) against Friday's settlement of $10.35, while April Palo Verde (PV) at $14.20-14.30 versus Friday's $14.45 close.
Both April power contracts will expire tomorrow.
The electricity complex would likely take cue from the natural gas futures today with the April Henry Hub contract expiring today, market sources said.
April Henry Hub natgas futures opened down 1.5 cents at $1.825 per million British thermal units.

Separately, Edison International said it planned to restore the 1,070 megawatt (MW) San Onofre 2 nuclear unit to service Wednesday after its startup was halted last Wednesday to repair a small leak in a valve in an internal water cooling system.
A 750 MW unit at the Four Corners coal-fired power plant in New Mexico was expected to restart last Saturday after being shut earlier this month for unplanned repair work.
Temperatures in the Northwest were predicted to run near normal today, but climb four to eight degrees Fahrenheit above norml by midweek.
Readings in the Southwest would average three to six degrees F Tuesday, and climb five to 10 degrees above seasonal norm for rest of the week.
